sentences.text: Revenue compounded 6.2% a year from $26.6 billion in FY2016 to $45.7 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F157], but the path was a cycle, not a straight line.
Revenue rose 25.6% in FY2018 to $37.4 billion [F3][D93], with the Wirtgen acquisition adding 12% to net sales that year [P72].
The peak was FY2023 at $61.3 billion [F8], followed by declines of 15.6% in FY2024 and 11.7% in FY2025 [D367][D412].
The FY2024 fall came from lower shipment volumes across every equipment segment, driven by rising grain stocks, lower commodity prices and elevated interest rates [P17].
Production Agriculture was the largest driver, at 37.1% of FY2025 revenue [D657], and it subtracted 7.0pp from growth that year [D659].
Its FY2025 decline came as sales volumes fell 30% in the U.S. and Canada, partly offset by a 22% increase in Brazil [P10].
Construction & Forestry, 25.5% of revenue [D889], fell 11.8% and subtracted 3.0pp [D890][D891].
Operating income grew faster than revenue over the window, at a 16.9% CAGR against 6.2% [F159][F157], but incremental margin turned negative in FY2024 at 41.1% [D388].
Diluted EPS compounded 16.1% against net income's 14.2% [F162][F160], as the diluted share count fell 1.9% in FY2025 [D427].
Operating margin was 17.5% in FY2024 [F30], above the 12.1% window median but below the 21.2% FY2023 high [D1335][D1334].
The FY2024 margin fell 3.7pp [D378], with SG&A costing 1.9pp and R&D 0.9pp [D391][D390].
FY2024 production costs were favorable on lower material and profit-sharing costs, partly offset by higher overhead from lower volumes [P16].
Net margin fell 2.7pp to 11.0% in FY2025 [F50][D422], and the 20.1% effective tax rate was below the 22.7% of FY2024 [D400][D355].
Net margin sat 3.7pp below operating margin in FY2024 [D1373], reflecting interest expense of $3.3 billion [X81].
Operating cash flow of $7.5 billion was 1.48x net income in FY2025 [F80][F40][D401], above the 1.17x window median [D1364].
The FY2025 inflow came from net income adjusted for non-cash provisions and a decrease in sales receivables, partly offset by an OPEB contribution [P5].
Free cash flow was $6.1 billion, a 13.4% margin [F100][D398], with capex at 3.0% of revenue and 0.61x D&A [D397][D403].
Free cash flow per dollar of net income was 1.21x [D402], in the 100th percentile against a 0.95x peer median [D1359][D1360].
Cash was $8.3 billion at FY2025 [F140], up 13.0% [D420], against $13.8 billion of current debt [X185].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2021 [X191], so net cash and debt-based peer ranks cannot be computed across the window [R9].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.9 billion were 46.9% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D409][D410], down from $8.6 billion and 121.9% in FY2023 [D319][D320].
Return on average equity fell to 20.6% [D411], in the 17th percentile against a 28.3% peer median [D1361][D1362].
Revenue fell in both FY2024 and FY2025 [F9][F10], a two-year decline [R1].
The FY2025 drop was concentrated in Production Agriculture, 37.1% of revenue and down 17.6% [D657][D658], on a 30% U.S. and Canada volume fall [P10].
Small Agriculture & Turf operating profit fell on lower volumes and higher tariffs, partly offset by price realization [P8].
The debt series breaks at FY2021, so net-cash and debt-growth comparisons across the window are unreliable [R9][X191].
Watch whether operating margin holds above the 12.1% window median [D1335] or falls toward the 9.7% FY2016 low [D1333], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Watch Production Agriculture revenue against the FY2025 level of $17.0 billion [S254]; a further decline would extend the two-year slide [R1].
Management forecasts lower FY2026 equipment operating cash flow, partly offset by inventory reductions [P6], so watch operating cash flow against the $7.5 billion FY2025 level [F80].
